text: Let f : [0,1] $\to$ R be such that f(xy) = f(x).f(y),  for all x, y $\in$ [0, 1], and f(0) $\neq$ 0. If y = y(x) satiesfies the differential equation, $\frac{dy}{dx}$ = f(x) with y(0) = 1, then y$\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )$ + y$\left (\frac{3}{4}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If f(xy) = f(x) f(y) $\forall$ x, y $\in$ R and f(0) $\neq$ 0

put x = y = 0

$\Rightarrow$  f(0) = [f(0)]$^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$  f(0) = 1

put y = 0 $\Rightarrow$ f(0) = f(x) f(0)

$\Rightarrow$ f(x) = 1

given that $\frac{dy}{dx}$ = f(x)

$\therefore$  $\frac{dy}{dx}$ = 1 $\Rightarrow$ y = x + k

given that y(0) = 1

$\therefore$  k = 1

hence y = x + 1

y$\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )$ + y$\left (\frac{3}{4}\right )$ = $\left (\frac{1}{4}+1\right )$ + $\left (\frac{3}{4}+1\right )$ = 3

text:
A data consists of n observations : $x_{1}, x_{2}, . . . . . . ., x_{n}$.    

If     $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}(x_{i}+1)^{2}=9n$    and 

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}(x_{i}-1)^{2}=5n,$ 

then the standard deviation of this data is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}(x_{i}+1)^{2}=9n$

$\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}^{2}+2\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}+n=9n...(1)$

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}(x_{i}-1)^{2}=5n$

$\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}^{2}-2\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}+n=5n...(2)$

Performing (1) + (2), we get

$2\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}^{2}+2n=14n$

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}^{2}=6n$

Performing (1) $-$ (2), we get

$\Rightarrow 4\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}=4n$

$\Rightarrow\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}x_{i}=n$

S.D($σ$)$=\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{n}-(x–)^{2}}$

$σ$ $=\sqrt{\frac{6n}{n}-(1)}$

$σ$ $=\sqrt{5}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: An urn contains 5 red and 2 green balls. A ball is drawn at random from the urn. If the drawn ball is green, then a red ball is added to the urn and if the drawn ball is red, then a green ball is added to the urn; the original ball is not returned to the urn. Now, a second ball is drawn at random from it. The probability that the second ball is red, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
5 Red and 2 green balls

P(one red ball) = $\frac{5}{7}$

P(one green ball) = $\frac{2}{7}$

Case I : 

If drawn ball is green than a red ball is added

$\left (\begin{array}{l} 6\mathrm{Re}d \\ 1~Green \end{array}\right )$ P (red ball) = $\frac{6}{7}$

Case II : 

If drawn ball is red than a green ball is added

$\left (\begin{array}{l} 4\mathrm{Re}d \\ 3~Green \end{array}\right )$ P (red ball) = $\frac{4}{7}$

$P (2^{nd}$ red ball) = $\frac{5}{7}$ $\times \frac{4}{7}+\frac{2}{7}\times \frac{6}{7}$ = $\frac{32}{49}$

text: If the lines x = ay + b,   z = cy + d  and x = a'z + b',  y = c'z + d'  are perpendicular,  then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equation of $1^{st}$ line is 

$\frac{x-b}{a}=\frac{y}{1}=\frac{z-d}{c}$

Dr's of $1^{st}$ line = ($a$, 1 , c)

Equation of $2^{nd}$ line is 

$\frac{x-b^{'}}{a^{'}}=\frac{y-b^{'}}{c^{'}}=\frac{z}{1}$

Dr's of $2^{nd}$ line = ($a^{'}$, c' , 1)

Lines are perpendicular, so the dot product of the Dr's of two lines are zero.

$\therefore$ $aa$' + c + c' = 0

text: If   $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{3}}\frac{\tan θ}{\sqrt{2k\sec θ}}dθ=1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},(k>0),$ then value of k is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{3}}\frac{\tan θ}{\sqrt{2k\sec θ}}dθ=1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},(k>0),$ 

$\Rightarrow \quad \int\limits _{0}^{π/3}\frac{\tan θ}{\sqrt{2k\sec θ}}dθ=1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(k>0)$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{2k}}\left (-2\sqrt{\cos θ}\right )_{0}^{π/3}=1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{2k}}\left (-\sqrt{2}+2\right )=1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sqrt{2}\left (\sqrt{2}-1\right )}{\sqrt{2k}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \quad k=2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
Let  $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\sqrt{2}\widehat{k},$   $\vec{b}=b_{1}\hat{i}+b_{2}\hat{j}+\sqrt{2}\widehat{k}$,    $\vec{c}=5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\sqrt{2}\widehat{k}$   be three vectors such that the projection vector of  $\vec{b}$  on  $\vec{a}$  is  $\vec{a}$.

solution.body:
Projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a}$ is $\vec{a}$

$\therefore$   $\frac{\vec{b}\cdot \vec{a}}{\left |\vec{a}\right |}=\left |\vec{a}\right |$

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{b_{1}+b_{2}+2}{2}=2$

$\Rightarrow$  $b_{1}+b_{2}=2....(1)$

and $\vec{a}$ + $\vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\left (\vec{a}+\vec{b}\right )\cdot \vec{c}=0$

$\Rightarrow$  $5(b_{1}+1)+(b_{2}+1)+\sqrt{2}\left (2\sqrt{2}\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow$  $5b_{1}+b_{2}+10=0......(2)$

solving (1) & (2)

$b_{1}$ $=$ $-$ 3  and  $b_{2}$ $=$ 5

$\Rightarrow$  $\left |\vec{b}\right |=\sqrt{9+25+2}=6$
